2_Introduction: The PSCs exhibited a superior PCE of 26.2531% (JSC: 26.511 mA/cm², VOC: 1.1942 V, FF: 82.9223%). For the perovskite film, 1.65 mol/L precursor solution was prepared according to the chemical formula of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0. Specifically, the perovskite precursor solution was first spun at 1000 rpm for 5 s, and then at 5500 rpm for 30 s. During the second step, 150 µL of CB as anti-solvent was quickly dripped onto the centre of the perovskite film 15 s before the end of the spin-coating process. Post-synthesis annealing at 110 °C for 15 min promoted uniform grain growth and optimal device characteristics.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cells arise from a precisely orchestrated interplay between compositional design, kinetic crystallization control, and intrinsic defect minimization—despite the absence of exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators in the reported protocol, the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ formulation leverages A-site cation entropy to stabilize the photoactive α-phase while suppressing halide vacancy formation and ion migration through enhanced Goldschmidt tolerance factor (≈0.92) and reduced lattice strain; the 1.65 mol/L precursor concentration balances nucleation density and mass transport during spin-coating, where the two-step spin protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 5 s) for uniform wet-film formation followed by high-speed (5500 rpm, 30 s) for rapid solvent expulsion—enables controlled supersaturation buildup, and the timed antisolvent quenching with 150 µL chlorobenzene delivered 15 s before spin termination triggers instantaneous nucleation at optimal supersaturation, yielding dense, pinhole-free films with large, oriented grains as confirmed by high-coverage optical imaging and uniform PL intensity mapping that evidences suppressed spatial heterogeneity in non-radiative recombination; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min drives Ostwald ripening without inducing PbI₂ segregation—XRD confirms complete phase purity with no residual PbI₂ peak at ~12.6° and narrow (001) FWHM, indicating low microstrain and high crystallinity—while time-resolved PL reveals a prolonged carrier lifetime (>1.2 µs) and steep initial decay slope, corroborating efficient radiative recombination and minimal trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall losses across the film; this synergistic crystallization pathway—governed by precursor stoichiometry, kinetic antisolvent intervention, and thermally tuned grain coalescence—collectively suppresses deep-level defects at grain boundaries and surfaces, enhances charge-carrier diffusion length, and improves interfacial energy alignment with adjacent charge transport layers, culminating in VOC of 1.1942 V, JSC of 26.511 mA/cm², FF of 82.9223%, and PCE of 26.2531%.
